title: White tie: what goes with the tailcoat
notes: Suitwerk Woche 1 (Vorlage 1.0). Thema E02 aus menswear_2026-11.research.json. Nur Aussagen aus S1-S3; Wiener Ballregeln nicht verallgemeinert (meist genügt Smoking), keine Rangfolge der Dresscodes als Fakt.

layout.description: What belongs to white tie? Debrett's describes a tailcoat with silk lapels, trousers with two braids, a white Marcella waistcoat, a wing collar and a white bow tie. The Vienna Opera Ball requires exactly that; at most balls, says austria.info, a dinner suit will do.

beats.spoken: The invitation says white tie. That means tails. But what really belongs, and what no longer does?

data.question: White tie: what goes with tails?

beats.spoken: You know black tie: dinner jacket, black bow tie. For the Vienna Opera Ball, that is not enough. The official site asks for a black tailcoat, a white shirt, a white bow tie and black patent shoes.

Debrett's, the British authority on etiquette, describes the tailcoat precisely: black and single-breasted, with silk-faced peak lapels, and worn open. The trousers carry two lines of braid down the outside seam.
Beneath, it turns white. On the left, black tie with a black bow. On the right, white tie: a low-cut white Marcella waistcoat, a stiff, detachable wing collar, and a narrow white bow, tied by hand.
Does every ball need tails? According to austria.info, only some, such as the Opera Ball. At most, a dinner suit is enough. And top hat and cane? Debrett's says these days, only on stage.
In short: the tailcoat is black, single-breasted and worn open, the trousers have two braids. Waistcoat and bow tie are white, the bow tied by hand. And tails are required only at some balls.

items.title: Required: some balls
items.sub: otherwise a dinner suit will do
